data.name: Atira
data.gender_notes: Atira is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Atir' meaning 'radiant' or 'shining', Atira is a popular name among Hindus, symbolizing the divine light and power of the deities. It is a name for a girl who is believed to bring joy, prosperity, and enlightenment to her family and loved ones. The name Atira carries the meaning “Radiant, Shining, Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Atira usually hope their child will grow to embody radiant, shining, light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine light and power
data.etymology: Atira belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Radiant, Shining, Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Atira total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spiritualism, the name Atira holds deep meaning. It represents the shining light and power of the divine, symbolizing hope, joy, and enlightenment. It is believed that the name bestows blessings of prosperity, happiness, and spiritual growth upon the child, making it a cherished name among Hindus.

historical_references.reference: Atira was a queen consort of the Shakambhari Chalukya king, Vijayaditya Siddeshvara (1127-1158 CE). She is mentioned in the inscription on the Raktasagara Tank at Gadag, Karnataka.

Another reference to Atira can be found in the Prabandha Samudracharya of the 13th century Kannada poet, Sarangapani. In this work, Atira is described as the queen of the Vijayanagara king, Veera Ballala I (1234-1268 CE).
